thread:
Sam (AE): Heads up — running a short POC with Orion Health next week. They want a quick perf baseline + burst test for their realtime triage product. Main asks: p50/p95/p99 latencies, sustained throughput, and burst behavior. Also price estimate for sustained 100qps with 2k token average and a 500qps 2-minute burst.

Priya (Sales Eng): Great. I can own the load plan and run the benchmark with our harness. Quick Q: which model variant are they targeting? quantized 4-bit or FP16? That changes numbers a lot.

Sam (AE): They said they want best-effort cost first, likely a gpt-like open model we ship (r-instruct-7b) in q4 quantized mode. Priority is latency.

Priya (Sales Eng): OK. Proposed plan:
1) Baseline - 50 qps sustained, 10 min, 2k avg tokens.
2) Scale sweep - 50 -> 200 -> 350 qps steps, 5 min each, to find knee.
3) Burst sims - 500 qps for 2 min, repeated 3x with 10m cool-down.
4) Tail analysis - capture p50/p90/p95/p99 and GPU %util + host metrics.

Also I'll pin model: r-instruct-7b@v2.1-quant. We'll record config: batch size=auto, max_seq=2048, kv_cache=true.

Ethan (SRE): Add these infra constraints: GPU pool = dedicated A100x2, batch latency cap = 200ms. Use prefix caching for repeated prompts. Monitor KV cache hit rate. If you use continuous batching, set max_batch_tokens=4096 to avoid token spill.

Priya (Sales Eng): Load generator snippet I'll run (locust wrapper + vegeta for concurrency):
```
vegeta attack -targets=targets.txt -rate=500 -duration=2m | vegeta report -type=json > burst_500_2m.json
# locust for sustained runs: locust -f locustfile.py --headless -u 200 -r 20 --run-time 10m
```
Targets will call our infer endpoint: POST /v1/generate with prompt payload (2k tokens average).

Sam (AE): Pricing question from procurement: what's the ballpark on monthly cost for 100qps sustained with those token sizes (production, hosted)? They want monthly commit estimate to compare to self-host.

Priya (Sales Eng): Rough calc: 100 qps * 3600 * 24 * 30 ~ 259M requests tokens per month. At ~2k tokens = 518B tokens. With hosted token rate for quantized 7B ~ $0.0000008 per token (example), estimate = 518B * 8e-7 ~ $414k/month. That's a raw engine-level estimate; we can compress via batching and prefix cache which typically drops billable tokens by ~20-40% for repeated contexts. I'll follow up with a more precise quote.

Nina (Customer Success): Heads-up: their security team flagged two blockers in the questionnaire: 1) data residency in EU, 2) KMS-backed key control and audit logs. For the POC they want to ensure telemetry doesn't leave their VPC.

Ethan (SRE): For EU residency and KMS we can run the POC on a dedicated EU Private node (private plane) — need SOW and a short MSA addendum. For the short run we can offer a dedicated test cluster in eu-west-1; will need their IP allowlist and a service account.

Priya (Sales Eng): For the benchmark let's capture these metrics per run: p50/p90/p95/p99, request throughput, GPU util, p99 GPU memory, CPU steal, avg tokens billed, cache hit rate, and error rate. I'll attach a results summary CSV afterward.

perf-ci-bot: Automated run complete: baseline_50qps_10m -> p50=38ms, p90=120ms, p95=210ms, p99=480ms, throughput=49.8 qps, GPU_util=62%, cache_hit=18% (logs: s3://redwood-perf/orion/2026-03-19/baseline_50.json).

Priya (Sales Eng): Nice first numbers. Next step: run scale sweep tomorrow morning (09:00 UTC). Can @Ethan confirm EU dedicated test cluster will be ready by then?

Ethan (SRE): I can provision the cluster. ETA 6 hours. I'll open a short runbook and the IP allowlist request.

Sam (AE): I'll update Orion Health with the test schedule and ask them to sign the quick addendum for EU test cluster. Also looping in procurement contacts.

Nina (Customer Success): I'll prep the security note and sample KMS config for them. Sam, can you get their expected retention window for logs? They might want 90 days.

Sam (AE): Will ask. Last item: if the burst shows 500 qps triggers fallback, what's our recommended fallback policy? Degrade to smaller model or queue?

Priya (Sales Eng): Recommend graceful degrade: 1) soft limit -> reduce max tokens to 1k, 2) if still overloaded spin up hot spare (dedicated burst capacity) or 3) fallback to r-instruct-3b quant which we already have warmed. We'll capture quality delta on a small eval set.

Ethan (SRE): Also enable a circuit-breaker at 800 qps to avoid GPU OOMs. We'll log any fallback events for postmortem.

perf-ci-bot: Post-run summary (scale_sweep): knee observed ~310 qps, p95 at knee ~260ms, beyond knee p99 increases sharply. Full report: s3://redwood-perf/orion/2026-03-19/scale_sweep_report.json

Sam (AE): Great thread. Priya — can you post the final CSV + 1-page writeup after the sweep so I can share with their CTO? If we can include the cost estimate variants (hosted vs dedicated vs private) that'd be ideal.

Priya (Sales Eng): Will do. I'll attach a 1-pager with recommended deployment for latency-first use: dedicated EU cluster + hot spare + quant profile; and three cost scenarios. Meeting to review with Orion scheduled: 2026-03-20 14:00 CET. :calendar: 

Ethan (SRE): I'll include the runbook and the ip/sa instructions in the doc.

Nina (Customer Success): I'll own consent note and KMS example.

Sam (AE): Thanks team :thumbsup: Let's get the sweep done tomorrow and finalize the quote.
